name: Chicken Manchurian
subtitle: fried chicken in a dark garlic and soy gravy, the dish that built Indian Chinese

image.credit: Abhinaba Basu from Redmond, United States

ingredients.note: the dish is built on garlic; do not reduce this

ingredients.qty: 500ml for deep frying, plus 3 tbsp for the gravy

prepNotes: Invented in Kolkata, not Manchuria. Nelson Wang is generally credited with it at a Bombay hotel in the 1970s.
Fry the chicken twice. The second fry is what keeps it crisp once the gravy is on it.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the egg, 3 tbsp cornflour, the maida, salt and pepper into a thick coating.
Deep fry on medium until pale gold, 4 minutes. Rest 5 minutes, then fry again on high for 1 minute.
steps.tip: The double fry is the whole technique. One fry and it goes soggy the moment it meets the sauce.

steps.text: In 3 tbsp oil, fry the garlic, ginger, green chilli and spring onion whites hard for 1 minute.
steps.tip: Hard and fast. Garlic browned slowly turns bitter.

steps.text: Add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and water. Bring to a boil.
Slake the remaining cornflour in cold water and stir it in until the sauce turns glossy and coats a spoon.
Fold in the chicken, toss for 30 seconds only, and finish with the spring onion greens.
steps.tip: Thirty seconds. Any longer and the crust you worked for is gone.

storage: Best within the hour, which is true of anything fried and sauced. It keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat in a hot pan, not a microwave.
